mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation and increases the attractiveness of equities relative to bonds, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward window, the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS decline is below 0.03 or the average return in periods of FEDFUNDS decline is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.0%, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which translates into positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint growth condition (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening supply conditions that may lead to recession fears, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, INDPRO decline does not lead to negative 20-day returns (returns positive in >50% of cases) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 5.0% signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) consistently indicates a healthy labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns following strong PAYEMS growth (e.g., >100k jobs) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising and CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, the market anticipates a recession due to aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 3.0) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, HOUST decline does not lead to negative 60-day returns (returns positive in >50% of cases) or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
